summary:
CHRONOS-102 is an interactive astronomy platform for exploring the infrared sky using NASA SPHEREx observations. It makes complex space-science data easier to access, compare, interpret, and share.

Users can search for an object by name or enter sky coordinates (RA/Dec), choose a field of view, and explore observations. Blink, Difference, Curtain, and Deep Co-add modes help compare visits and inspect possible changes. The application displays SPHEREx’s six detector arrays and supports pixel-level spectral inspection across 102 near-infrared channels, showing how a selected pixel’s signal changes with wavelength.

CHRONOS-102 adds context through astronomical resources including Gaia DR3, WISE, CatWISE, NEOWISE, and NASA JPL data. Users can inspect source information, compare observations, and export discovery cards to document and share investigations.

The project includes reproducible demonstration fields based on saved real SPHEREx archive responses. Live searches depend on NASA/IPAC archive availability; the interface distinguishes real archive data from simulated displays and failed queries. CHRONOS-102 supports visual exploration and candidate inspection, not automatic confirmation of discoveries.

By combining image comparison, spectral inspection, and catalogue context in one web application, CHRONOS-102 aims to make infrared astronomy more approachable for researchers, students, educators, and citizen scientists, encouraging wider engagement with NASA mission data.
details:
CHRONOS-102: Interactive Infrared Discovery Engine

Exploring Moving and Changing Infrared Sources Using NASA SPHEREx

Team Name: ProximaZZZ

1. PROJECT DETAILS

Project Overview

CHRONOS-102 is a browser-based interactive infrared astronomy platform developed to investigate moving and changing astronomical sources using NASA SPHEREx observations and complementary space-science datasets.

The project addresses an important challenge in astronomical discovery: potentially interesting objects are difficult to identify using a single image, catalogue, or wavelength. An astronomical source may appear ordinary in one observation but demonstrate unusual brightness, position, or spectral behavior when observations from different epochs and astronomical surveys are compared.

CHRONOS-102 approaches this problem through a combination of spatial analysis, temporal comparison, spectral investigation, astrometric measurements, and independent catalogue verification.

The platform is designed to make these complex scientific processes accessible through an interactive interface where users can search astronomical objects, explore infrared observations, investigate unusual signals, and evaluate potential candidates.

How CHRONOS-102 Works

1. Interactive Astronomical Field Exploration

Users can search for astronomical objects by name or enter their right ascension and declination coordinates.

The platform resolves object positions and allows users to explore selected regions of the sky through an interactive astronomical interface.

Users can adjust the field of view, select different objects, inspect available survey images, and initiate investigations of particular sky regions.

2. SPHEREx 102-Band Infrared Exploration

CHRONOS-102 integrates NASA SPHEREx archive data to explore observations across 102 infrared spectral channels, covering approximately 0.75–5.0 micrometers.

The system is designed to retrieve available real SPHEREx observations, examine FITS image products, and investigate spectral information associated with selected positions.

The platform also provides a simulated field environment for demonstrating its discovery pipeline when suitable real observations are unavailable. Real observations and simulated data are identified separately.

3. Multi-Epoch Observation Comparison

One of the main capabilities of CHRONOS-102 is comparing observations from different visits.

The platform provides several interactive analysis modes:

  • Blink comparison between two observations.
  • Difference E2−E1 analysis.
  • Deep co-add visualization.
  • Curtain comparison.
  • Multi-array image combination.

These tools help users investigate changes in source brightness and apparent position between observations.

4. Moving-Source and Anomaly Investigation

CHRONOS-102 includes an anomaly and dipole scanner designed to investigate potential moving or changing astronomical sources.

It uses image differences, source-position comparisons, and astrometric information to identify interesting candidates.

The platform also incorporates Gaia DR3 reference information and point-spread-function subtraction approaches to reduce the contribution of static stars during image analysis.

5. Independent Astronomical Verification

An unusual signal does not automatically represent a new astronomical discovery. It may correspond to an already-known star, a Solar System object, an instrumental artifact, or a background source.

CHRONOS-102 addresses this challenge through independent astronomical catalogue comparisons.

The integrated resources include:

  • ESA Gaia DR3 for stellar positions and astrometric information.
  • NASA AllWISE for infrared catalogue comparisons.
  • NASA NEOWISE for multi-epoch infrared observations.
  • CatWISE2020 for additional infrared source information.
  • NASA JPL Solar System Dynamics for checking known Solar System objects.

Cross-verification helps users investigate candidate identities and distinguish potentially interesting signals from previously known objects.

6. Spectral Analysis and Infrared Diagnostics

The platform includes an interactive spectral viewer for examining brightness variations across infrared wavelengths.

It provides diagnostic visualizations associated with:

  • Water (H₂O).
  • Methane (CH₄).
  • Carbon dioxide (CO₂).
  • Carbon monoxide (CO).
  • Thermal dust emission.

These wavelength regions provide useful scientific context for investigating different astronomical environments and possible source characteristics.

The spectral analysis is intended as an exploratory diagnostic rather than definitive chemical identification.

7. Citizen-Science Discovery Ledger

CHRONOS-102 includes a collaborative discovery ledger where users can flag potential candidates, submit observations, and participate in candidate evaluation.

Users can also generate discovery cards, export scan reports, and share investigation results.

This feature transforms the platform from a simple astronomical visualization tool into an interactive citizen-science environment.

8. Planet X Investigation Mode

The platform includes a schematic Planet X investigation environment for exploring how researchers might investigate a hypothetical distant moving object.

It demonstrates concepts such as apparent motion, parallax, infrared investigation, and comparison between observation epochs.

This is a hypothetical investigation and simulation feature, not a claim that Planet X has been discovered or detected by CHRONOS-102.

2. MAIN FEATURES

Feature 1: Real SPHEREx Data Explorer

Integrates NASA SPHEREx DR1 and QR3 archive resources through NASA IRSA.

Supports astronomical FITS products, spatial coordinate transformations, image retrieval, and spectral exploration.

Feature 2: Multi-Epoch Motion Detection

Compares astronomical observations from different visits to investigate changes in source position and brightness.

Feature 3: 102-Band Spectral Explorer

Provides interactive visualization of infrared brightness across SPHEREx spectral channels and wavelength-specific diagnostic filters.

Feature 4: Anomaly and Dipole Scanner

Investigates potential moving sources, transient signals, and unusual image differences using source subtraction and detection visualizations.

Feature 5: Cross-Catalogue Verification

Uses independent astronomical resources, including Gaia, WISE, NEOWISE, CatWISE2020, and JPL, to investigate candidate identities.

Feature 6: Multiple Visualization Modes

Provides different ways to examine astronomical observations:

  • Blink.
  • Difference E2−E1.
  • Deep co-add.
  • Curtain.
  • False-colour RGB.
  • Single-channel visualization.
  • Multi-array combination.

Feature 7: Citizen-Science Discovery Ledger

Allows users to flag candidates, record observations, participate in collaborative evaluation, and export investigation reports.

Feature 8: Discovery Card Export

Creates shareable discovery cards containing relevant candidate information and investigation results.

Feature 9: Planet X Scenario

Provides a hypothetical investigation environment for demonstrating how distant moving-object detection and parallax analysis can be explored.

Feature 10: Interactive Astronomical Dashboard

Combines object search, coordinate selection, field exploration, spectral visualization, source analysis, and discovery tools in one interface.

3. INNOVATION AND ORIGINALITY

CHRONOS-102 introduces a unified approach to exploring moving and changing infrared sources by combining several astronomical investigation techniques in one interactive platform.

1. Combining Spatial, Temporal and Spectral Analysis

Many introductory astronomical tools focus on displaying images or catalogue information. CHRONOS-102 combines three complementary dimensions of investigation:

Spatial Analysis: Where is the source located?

Temporal Analysis: How does its position or brightness change between observations?

Spectral Analysis: How does its infrared brightness vary across different wavelengths?

Combining these dimensions provides a more comprehensive way to investigate unusual astronomical sources.

2. Multi-Survey Scientific Verification

An unusual signal may already correspond to a known astronomical object.

CHRONOS-102 addresses this challenge by comparing candidate information against multiple independent astronomical catalogues and resources.

This makes candidate investigation more scientifically informed than relying on a single image or survey.

3. Lightweight Real-Data Access

A major technical innovation in the implementation is its approach to accessing large SPHEREx FITS products.

Instead of downloading complete astronomical image files whenever possible, the SPHEREx engine uses HTTP byte-range requests to retrieve selected FITS headers and relevant image data.

The implementation also incorporates:

  • Custom FITS header parsing.
  • TAN-SIP celestial coordinate transformations.
  • WAVE-TAB wavelength interpolation.
  • Astrometric proper-motion calculations.
  • Selective astronomical image retrieval.

This approach is designed to reduce unnecessary data transfer and make interactive astronomical exploration more practical.

4. Scientific Processing in an Interactive Environment

CHRONOS-102 combines astronomical data access with interactive investigation tools.

Users can move between image comparison, spectral inspection, catalogue verification, and candidate reporting without needing to operate separate astronomy applications for every step.

5. Citizen Science as Part of Discovery

The discovery ledger makes the platform more than a visualization tool.

It creates a structured environment where users can identify interesting signals, record observations, and contribute to candidate evaluation.

6. Real Observations and Simulation Together

The platform includes both real astronomical data and a simulation environment.

This allows users to understand the analysis methods and experiment with hypothetical scenarios even when suitable real observations are unavailable.

Real observations and simulated demonstrations are kept distinguishable to prevent hypothetical results from being confused with scientific evidence.

4. CREATIVITY AND CREATIVE APPROACH

The creative concept behind CHRONOS-102 is to transform infrared astronomical investigation into an interactive discovery experience.

Rather than presenting astronomical data as static images and charts, the platform allows users to explore a region of the sky, compare observations, investigate unusual signals, examine spectral characteristics, and independently verify possible candidates.

Several creative elements make this experience distinctive.

1. Dipole Ruler

An interactive measurement concept that helps users investigate apparent displacement between earlier and later source positions.

2. Blink and Difference Visualization

Switching between observation epochs makes subtle changes easier to investigate and understand.

3. Spectral Sound Visualization

The platform includes an option to represent spectral information through sound, providing an alternative way to experience astronomical measurements.

4. Molecular Diagnostic Filters

Dedicated wavelength filters help users explore infrared regions associated with water, methane, carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide, and thermal dust.

5. Planet X Scenario

A hypothetical investigation demonstrates how researchers might explore a distant moving object using parallax and infrared observations.

6. Citizen Discovery Experience

Users can contribute candidate flags, record investigation details, and generate shareable discovery records rather than simply viewing scientific results.

The overall design aims to make advanced astronomical concepts approachable without removing the scientific context behind the data.

5. TECHNOLOGIES AND TOOLS USED

CHRONOS-102 was developed using a combination of web technologies, scientific Python libraries, astronomical archives, and data-processing techniques.

Frontend Technologies

  • HTML5.
  • CSS3.
  • JavaScript.
  • Interactive astronomical visualization components.
  • Canvas-based image rendering and interaction.

Backend Technologies

  • Python.
  • FastAPI.
  • REST API architecture.
  • Requests for external archive communication.
  • JSON-based data exchange.

Scientific Computing and Processing

  • NumPy for numerical calculations and image processing.
  • Custom FITS header and binary-data parsing.
  • TAN-SIP celestial coordinate transformations.
  • WAVE-TAB wavelength interpolation.
  • Astrometric proper-motion propagation.
  • Image differencing and co-addition.
  • Source analysis and visualization.

Astronomical Data Sources

NASA Resources

  • NASA SPHEREx.
  • NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA).
  • NASA AllWISE.
  • NASA NEOWISE.
  • NASA JPL Solar System Dynamics.
  • NASA SkyView.

Additional Astronomical Resources

  • ESA Gaia DR3.
  • CatWISE2020.
  • CDS HiPS2FITS.

Data Infrastructure

  • IRSA SIA2 and TAP archive interfaces.
  • Public AWS S3 SPHEREx archive access.
  • HTTP Range requests for partial FITS retrieval.
  • Local JSON caching.
  • CSV and JSON export.
6. SCIENTIFIC IMPACT AND IMPORTANCE

CHRONOS-102 aims to make infrared astronomical exploration more accessible by bringing multiple datasets and analysis techniques into one interactive environment.

Its potential contributions include:

  1. Helping users investigate moving and changing infrared sources across multiple observation epochs.
  2. Encouraging comparison of independent astronomical catalogues before treating a signal as a potential discovery.
  3. Making SPHEREx spectral information more approachable through interactive visualization.
  4. Introducing students and astronomy enthusiasts to scientific concepts such as proper motion, infrared spectroscopy, image subtraction, and astrometric verification.
  5. Encouraging citizen-science participation through candidate reporting and collaborative evaluation.
  6. Demonstrating how large astronomical archives can be accessed and explored using efficient data-retrieval techniques.

The project is designed as an exploratory scientific and educational platform. Its findings are candidate investigations, not automatically confirmed astronomical discoveries.

7. CONCLUSION

CHRONOS-102 is an attempt to make infrared astronomical discovery more interactive, accessible, and scientifically connected.

By bringing together NASA SPHEREx observations, multi-epoch comparison, 102-band spectral exploration, astrometric investigation, independent catalogue verification, and citizen-science participation, the platform provides a unified environment for exploring moving and changing astronomical sources.

Its central idea is simple: an astronomical object should not be investigated through a single image alone. Its location, behavior over time, infrared characteristics, and relationship with previously known objects all provide important clues.

CHRONOS-102 brings these clues together in one place and invites users to participate in the process of scientific exploration.

Our vision is to turn astronomical data into an accessible discovery experience, where anyone can explore the infrared universe, investigate unusual signals, and contribute to the search for answers.

CHRONOS-102 — Explore the Invisible. Discover the Unexpected.

USE OF GENERATIVE AI:
Generative AI tools (Claude) were used as development assistants for research assistance, code drafting and debugging, UI design, and writing and editing project documentation. The tools are not presented as a source of astronomical observations or scientific discoveries. Scientific data and results are based on astronomical archive resources and project processing.
